answer: A harbor of trust forms when every agent must lock a refundable stake before trading: the bond sits in escrow, and any proven fraud slashes it, so spinning up a thousand fake identities costs a thousand stakes instead of nothing. Reputation then grows like a nebula, slow, visible, and hard to fake, because each identity's history is anchored to capital it can lose. Newcomers start with velvet-gloved limits, small trades only, until their stake-backed record earns wider access. Sybils stay expensive and small; honest agents compound trust cheaply.
